openings.claim: Separate lateral location from seal compression using two removable padded strip-jaw clamps whose bolt shanks provide opposing hatch-edge stops. Feasibility remains uncertain because rim access, hatch thickness and bolt reach are unspecified.
openings.delta: Change the sideways-load dependency from hatch/seal friction to edge contact carried through aluminum strips into the rim; use modest, balanced jaw preload for retention. The nearest rival is friction-only retention obtained by tightening the left corner.
openings.prediction: If edge location carries the pull, movement should remain within 1 mm without escalating corner pressure; the rival predicts improvement principally with increased preload. Persistent opposite-corner lift, stop migration or slip above 1 mm defeats the proposed separation. The final right-side card may expose rocking despite adequate lateral restraint.
openings.probe: First inspect accessible rim lips, strip overlap, bolt reach and recoverable placement without altering hatch, rim or seal. Proceed only if two opposing jaw pairs and edge-stop contacts can be formed using the supplied strips, bolts and pads. Drill/cut strips only; tether removable parts with cord. Mark position. Use ten closure/pull trials with ten opening cycles, timing reopening each time; disturb the final closure with the supplied right-contact card. Measure position, corner lift and response to the supplied 20 N pull; inspect seal after each cycle. Reserve two trials for a reversible preload comparison if time permits. Stop at new tears or threatened permanent deformation. Inability to assemble safely is a resource defeat, not evidence against the mechanism.
assumptions: Accessible rim geometry and supplied bolt lengths permit padded jaws and edge contacts.
Fabrication fits ninety minutes and ten cycles fit twenty minutes; neither capacity is established.
Edge-contact geometry permits full opening after clamps are released and one-person reopening within thirty seconds.

assessment: One geometry-dependent probe, not deployment. Success requires every stated outcome and hard constraint, including the disturbed final closure; a stop limit alone supplies no feasibility evidence.
